rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is empty, so the first experiment should establish a baseline by testing a simple rna_only model with singleprofile and pca_n2000 encoder. This clarifies the baseline performance of the RNA representation without image data, isolating the effect of the RNA encoder and profile setting. It is the best use of the first experiment to inform subsequent comparisons of more complex configurations.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (singleprofile, RNA-only) achieves 0.4849 validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching to multiprofile (profile_setting=multiprofile) improves performance while keeping RNA_encoder=pca_n2000 and image_encoder=None, isolating the effect of profile aggregation. It balances exploration of profile settings with minimal changes, addressing uncertainty about whether multiprofile configurations could yield better results without complicating other factors.

Existing evidence shows that multiprofile RNA-only models (config_002) outperform singleprofile ones (config_001) with 0.5907 accuracy. This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool (config_002) with transformer aggregation improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It directly extends the promising multiprofile direction while maintaining other settings, balancing exploitation of known effectiveness with exploration of architectural choices.

Existing evidence shows multiprofile with avgpool aggregation (config_002, 0.5907 accuracy) outperforms singleprofile and transformer aggregation. This experiment tests replacing pca_n2000 RNA encoder with scvi_n200 in the multiprofile/avgpool setup, isolating the impact of RNA encoder choice. It builds on the promising multiprofile direction while exploring a key design decision (encoder type) with minimal changes, balancing exploitation of strong evidence and exploration of critical parameters.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 (config_005) outperforms pca_n2000 (config_002) when using multiprofile. This experiment tests whether scvi_n200's performance advantage persists with singleprofile, isolating the impact of profile setting. It directly addresses uncertainty about whether profile configuration is critical when using advanced encoders, while keeping other factors constant.

Existing evidence shows that scvi_n200 RNA encoder and avgpool aggregation (config_005) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.6501) among rna_only models. This experiment tests combining these effective components with multimodal fusion (concat) using resnet50 image encoder, which has shown strong performance in image-only models (config_010-012). It clarifies whether multimodal integration improves performance while isolating the effect of fusion and image modality, balancing exploitation of proven components with exploration of multimodal benefits.

Existing evidence shows that config_005 (rna_only with scvi_n200 and avgpool) achieves the highest accuracy so far (0.650). The next step is to test whether multimodal approaches with scvi_n200 RNA encoder and resnet50 image encoder can match or exceed this performance. Config_031 tests the same RNA/image encoder pair as config_030 but uses weighted fusion instead of concat, isolating the effect of fusion strategy. This comparison helps determine if weighted fusion improves performance over simple concatenation in multimodal settings, while building on the strong foundation of scvi_n200 and resnet50.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 and resnet50, weighted fusion, and avgpool aggregation (config_031) achieve high accuracy (0.6776). This experiment tests whether replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (config_033) further improves performance, isolating the effect of aggregation method. It balances exploitation of the promising multimodal direction with exploration of critical design choices.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests replacing the RNA encoder with scgpt while keeping other components identical, isolating the impact of the RNA encoder choice. This addresses uncertainty about whether scgpt (a more complex encoder) could further improve performance, aligning with the principle of testing critical design choices when evidence is strong.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with scvi_n200 RNA encoder, resnet50 image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (config_033) achieve the highest validation accuracy (0.713). This experiment tests whether replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more complex image encoder) while keeping aggregation and fusion methods the same isolates the impact of the image encoder choice. This comparison is critical to determine if upgrading the image encoder further improves performance, leveraging the strong evidence from config_033.
